leads.name: Northfield churchyard yew (St Laurence)
leads.reason: One source only (Ancient Yew Group tree 7124, 'Notable', girth 400 cm at 1 m, taken from Street View and unverified, earliest mention a 1921 photograph). No age basis, no photo, no coordinate beyond churchyard grid ref SP0255079342. Churchyard public. Could ship as approximate with location_site if a second source or a Geograph photo of the yew turns up.
leads.how_to_recognise: A twisted yew at the top of the steps leading into St Laurence church (AYG Street View note).

leads.name: Cofton Hackett fallen yew (St Michael and All Angels)
leads.city: Birmingham (day trip, Cofton Hackett, Worcestershire; transport time not verified)
leads.reason: AYG class 'Ancient', girth 5-7 m, fallen male yew SW of the 14th-century church, visited 2002 (Tim Hills); 'reputed more than 800 years old' per a 1946 rector quote relayed by AYG text on a blog mirror. One source, last visit 2002, not alive-checked, outside the city, 30-minute public transport not confirmed.
leads.how_to_recognise: Fallen, horse-shoe shaped yew lying SW of the church, per AYG.
